overview: The U.S. Merchant Marine Academy in Kings Point, New York, is a federal service academy run by the Department of Transportation that trains officers for the nation's commercial shipping fleet. This bill lets the Transportation Secretary set up a government-owned nonprofit corporation to raise money for and support the academy's sports teams, similar to arrangements at other service academies. The corporation could sign contracts with the department, lease unused academy property for up to five years, take over the assets of the existing fund that supports athletics, and handle licensing and sponsorship deals using the academy's name and logos, with limits meant to avoid conflicts of interest. The department could also accept money from the NCAA, athletic conferences, ticket sales and game fees, and keep trademark licensing fees, all to be spent on academy athletics and recruiting. The Senate passed it on August 6, 2026, and as of August 10, 2026, it was being held at the desk in the House.
for: Supporters say the bill gives the academy the same flexible tools other service academies use to fund their sports programs, bringing in outside money without new taxpayer spending.
against: Critics say allowing sole-source contracts, sponsorship deals and private fundraising tied to a federal agency raises the risk of conflicts of interest and weakens normal government contracting rules.
